title: Rational split realization of a finite reduced root datum
statement: Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ be a finite reduced root datum with the lattice, reflection and reducedness axioms of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with no base specified. There exists a split realization $(G_{\mathbf Q},T_{\mathbf Q}=D_{\mathbf Q}(M))$ over the field $\mathbf Q$ of rational numbers, in the sense of that definition with the base and pinning forgotten. In particular $G_{\mathbf Q}$ is smooth affine of finite presentation with connected reductive geometric fibres, $T_{\mathbf Q}$ is a closed fibrewise maximal torus, and its torus coaction has exactly the root support $\Phi$, coroots $\Phi^\vee$, free rank-one root lines and zero tangent summand $\operatorname{Lie}(T_{\mathbf Q})$, all with the specified character-lattice identification. Roots need not span $M$; empty roots and rank zero are allowed. This asserts realization over $\mathbf Q$ itself, not just over an algebraic closure or a number-field extension.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.12, printed pp.211--212: complex realization, spreading to a number field, and pinned Galois descent to Q. Read online; local PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states rational reductive-group realization.

proof.text: First pass from the simultaneous-reflection convention of the hypothesis to the finite-Weyl-group convention: [lem-sfb-finite-root-datum-weyl-group] applies to the given lattice and the finite corresponding root and coroot sets. Fix an algebraic closure $\mathbf Q\to\overline{\mathbf Q}$, which exists by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and identify $\mathbf Q$ with its image. Now [lem-sfb-root-datum-realization], with $F=\overline{\mathbf Q}$, produces a connected reductive group $G$ over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ with a split maximal torus $S$ and the specified character-lattice, root and coroot identification. This plays the role of the complex realization at the start of Conrad's proof: any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero serves, and $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ needs no separate fact about $\mathbf C$. It is not yet a rational realization.

Use character antiduality to identify $S$ with $T=D_{\overline{\mathbf Q}}(M)$; a basis of $M$ turns $T\subseteq G$ into a closed subgroup immersion $j:\mathbf G_m^r\hookrightarrow G$, $r=\operatorname{rank}M$. The group $G$ is smooth, connected and affine of finite type; [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] over the Noetherian field and the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of affine morphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] make it of finite presentation. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-fibre-openness] to $\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and its only point $s$: the geometric fibre over the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ of $\kappa(s)$ is $G$ itself, which is reductive with maximal torus $j$. Hence for every algebraically closed $\Omega$ with a homomorphism $\overline{\mathbf Q}\to\Omega$, $G_\Omega^0$ is reductive and $j_\Omega$ is a maximal torus of $G_\Omega^0$. As $G$ is connected with the rational identity point, [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $G_\Omega$ connected, so $G_\Omega=G_\Omega^0$. Thus $G$ is reductive over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ in the sense of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with all its geometric fibres, and every geometric fibre of $T$ is a maximal torus.

The Borel-pair theorem supplies a pair $(B\prime,T\prime)$ in $G$. By [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] choose $g$ with $gT\prime g^{-1}=T$ and put $B=gB\prime g^{-1}$; conjugation preserves smoothness, connectedness, solvability and its maximality, so $B$ is a Borel containing the specified $T$. The Borel-pair theorem now supplies its positive roots and simple base $\Delta$. By the preceding step the arbitrary-base root-line theorem applies to $(G,T)$: it identifies the zero weight with $\operatorname{Lie}(T)$, and its base-change comparison $\Omega\otimes\mathfrak g_m\simeq(\mathfrak g_\Omega)_m$ shows that the roots of every geometric fibre are those of $(G,T)$ itself, namely $\Phi$, with one-dimensional root spaces; the torus-weight decomposition has no other weights. Its relative coroot $\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_m\to T$ is a constant monomial map whose fibre over $\overline{\mathbf Q}$ is the canonical coroot, the prescribed one by step 1, and whose base change to each $\Omega$ is the canonical coroot there, so every geometric fibre has the prescribed coroots. Choose a nonzero $X_\alpha$ in each simple-root line. Over the field these are free generators, giving a pinned split realization $P_{\overline{\mathbf Q}}$ in the stated definition without a root-spanning hypothesis.

Apply [lem-sfb-split-reductive-finite-type-spreading] to $\mathbf Q\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}$ and $P_{\overline{\mathbf Q}}$. Obtain a nonzero finite-type $\mathbf Q$-subalgebra $A\subset\overline{\mathbf Q}$ carrying $P_A$. Choose a maximal ideal of $A$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field] its residue field $F_0$ is finite over $\mathbf Q$. It is separable: an irreducible polynomial in characteristic zero has nonzero derivative of smaller degree and hence no common factor with its derivative. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-galois-receiving-separable-extensions] to the one extension $F_0/\mathbf Q$, obtaining a finite Galois $F/\mathbf Q$ receiving $F_0$. Pull back $P_A$ through $A\to F_0\to F$ using [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change]. This gives a pinned split $P$ over $F$ of the original based datum, even though the first map is nonflat.

Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Gal}(F/\mathbf Q)$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma$, pullback along the automorphism $\gamma:F\to F$ gives a pinned split group ${}^\gamma P$. By base-change compatibility it has the same root labels, coroots and lattice $M$, and simple-root vectors ${}^\gamma X_\alpha$. In coordinates the canonical identification of its torus with $D_F(M)$ fixes each monomial $e_m$ and applies $\gamma$ only to coefficients. Thus the identification of the two based data is the identity on $M$, including its central directions.

Apply [lem-sfb-split-central-isogeny-lifting] with lattice map $1_M$ to ${}^\gamma P$ and $P$, forgetting pinnings. Obtain an isomorphism $f_\gamma:{}^\gamma G\to G$ equal to the identity monomial map on tori. Its differential sends ${}^\gamma X_\alpha$ to $c_\alpha X_\alpha$ for some $c_\alpha\in F^\times$. The simple roots are a $\mathbf Z$-basis of $Q=\mathbf Z\Phi$: independence is part of the base axiom, and every root is an integral combination of simple roots. Consequently there is a unique homomorphism $Q\to F^\times$ sending each $\alpha\in\Delta$ to $c_\alpha^{-1}$. By [lem-sfb-adjoint-torus-root-coordinates] its element $t_\gamma\in D_F(Q)(F)$ acts by these scalars. Then $a_\gamma=c_{t_\gamma}\circ f_\gamma$ matches all simple-root vectors. It is unique: any second such isomorphism differs by a unique element of $D_F(Q)(F)$; matching the vectors makes its values on the basis $\Delta$ all $1$, so that element is the identity.

Both $a_{\gamma\delta}$ and $a_\gamma\circ{}^\gamma a_\delta$ map ${}^{\gamma\delta}P$ to $P$, induce $1_M$, and carry every ${}^{\gamma\delta}X_\alpha$ to $X_\alpha$. The uniqueness just proved gives $a_{\gamma\delta}=a_\gamma\circ{}^\gamma a_\delta$, with the canonical identification of iterated scalar twists. Likewise $a_1=1$. Hence these maps are a Galois descent datum on the group and its specified torus. This proves the cocycle rather than assuming chosen isomorphisms automatically satisfy it.

Write $B=F[G]$ and translate group maps to Hopf maps using [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. The preceding cocycle gives a semilinear $\Gamma$-action preserving the Hopf operations. By [lem-sfb-galois-hopf-algebra-descent], $B_0=B^\Gamma$ is a finitely generated commutative Hopf $\mathbf Q$-algebra and $F\otimes_{\mathbf Q}B_0\simeq B$. Set $G_{\mathbf Q}=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ with the descended group law. The torus restriction $B\to F[M]$ is equivariant, where the latter has coefficient action only. Its invariant algebra is $\mathbf Q[M]$: comparing coefficients in its monomial basis says exactly that every coefficient is fixed by $\Gamma$. The same descent equivalence on morphisms therefore produces $T_{\mathbf Q}=D_{\mathbf Q}(M)\to G_{\mathbf Q}$, whose extension to $F$ is the specified torus inclusion.

The single map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Q$ is an fpqc cover: field extension is faithfully flat, its spectra each have one point, and this is a map of affines. Smoothness descends by [lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent], and the torus inclusion is closed by [lem-pc-fpqc-descend-closed-immersion]. The group is affine and finite type by construction; [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] gives local finite presentation over the Noetherian field, and an affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so this is finite presentation. For any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\mathbf Q$, choose a $\mathbf Q$-embedding $F\to\Omega$ by successively choosing roots of the minimal polynomials of finitely many field generators. Then $(G_{\mathbf Q},T_{\mathbf Q})_\Omega$ is the base change of $P$ with its pinning forgotten. By [lem-sfb-pinned-split-root-base-change] its group is connected reductive and its torus is maximal with precisely the prescribed roots and coroots.

Finally apply [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] over $\mathbf Q$ to this reductive group and closed fibrewise maximal split torus. Its tangent comparison identifies the weight spaces after extension to $\Omega$ with those just obtained from $P$; hence the nonzero root lines over $\mathbf Q$ have dimension one, and every other nonzero weight is zero. By [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] the full torus coaction is their direct sum with the zero weight, identified with $\operatorname{Lie}(T_{\mathbf Q})$. A one-dimensional vector space over $\mathbf Q$ is a free rank-one module. Together these are exactly the conditions for a split realization in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. When $\Phi=\varnothing$ the base and all pinning choices are empty, $Q=0$ and the correction automorphism is the identity; rank-zero and toral data pass through the same argument.
